results.result: In Shp2-deficient livers following partial hepatectomy (PHx), actively dividing hepatocytes form distinctive clusters characterized by upregulated CD133 expression while remaining negative for other progenitor cell markers. These CD133+ colonies appear transiently, expand over 3 weeks, and compensate for impaired proliferative capacity in CD133− hepatocytes.
results.evaluation: Claims C2, C3, C30, C31, C43-C53 collectively demonstrate through immunostaining (C44, C48, C49), time-course analysis (C50, C51), and liver/body weight measurements (C52) that Shp2-deficient hepatocytes form CD133+ proliferative clusters. The data show significantly higher Ki67+ percentages in CD133+ areas (C49), absence of other stem cell markers (C48), and transient appearance (C50, C60). The interpretation that CD133+ cells compensate for impaired proliferation (C53) is supported by similar liver/body weight ratios between SKO and WT mice (C52).

results.result: CD133+ hepatocyte colonies display tight E-cadherin-mediated cell-cell contacts with CD133 localized to the apical side. These colonies contain smaller, compact hepatocytes that express mature hepatocyte markers (HNF4α) but lack oval cell markers (EpCAM, AFP, Sox9), indicating they are mature hepatocytes rather than progenitor cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C54-C71 provide converging evidence from immunostaining (C54, C55, C64, C66, C67, C70), immunoblotting (C64, C65, C66, C68, C69, C70), and histological analysis (C57, C67) that CD133+ colonies consist of mature hepatocytes. The absence of oval cell markers (C66, C67) combined with expression of mature hepatocyte markers (C70) and lack of oval cell morphology (C67) strongly support the conclusion that these are mature hepatocytes (C71), not progenitor cells.

results.result: Clonal tracing experiments using GFP-labeled hepatocytes demonstrate that CD133+ colonies originate from multiple heterogeneous mature hepatocytes (~10 cells initially) that proliferate more actively within colonies than outside. Colony expansion occurs through internal cell division rather than continuous recruitment from surrounding tissue.
results.evaluation: Claims C72-C86 present clonal tracing data showing colonies contain both GFP+ and GFP− cells (C73), indicating multiple origins. Quantitative analysis demonstrates higher proliferation within colonies (C76), lack of recruitment at colony edges (C74), and estimation of ~10 initial hepatocytes (C78). In vitro experiments (C81, C82) confirm the phenotype. The presence of mononuclear and binuclear cells (C80) further supports heterogeneous origins. The conclusion that colonies form from heterogeneous mature hepatocytes (C79, C86) is well-supported by the collective data.

results.result: CD133+ proliferating hepatocyte clusters are induced in multiple liver injury models (CCl4, PHx) and genetic backgrounds (Shp2-deficient, MET-deficient), indicating CD133 induction is a general response to impaired proliferative signaling rather than specific to a particular gene deletion or injury type.
results.evaluation: Claims C87-C93 demonstrate CD133+ cluster formation across different injury models (CCl4: C88, C89, C90; PHx: C92) and genetic backgrounds (Shp2-deficient: C88; MET-deficient: C92, C33). The consistency across models supports the conclusion that CD133 induction is a response to impaired proliferative signaling (C93, C95) rather than model-specific. The data from CCl4 experiments (C88-C91) and MET-deficient mice (C92) provide independent validation of the phenotype observed in Shp2-deficient livers.

results.result: Pharmaceutical inhibition of the RTK-Ras-Erk pathway (using Shp2 or MEK inhibitors) rapidly induces CD133 expression in diverse cancer cell lines from multiple species and organs, independent of other stem cell markers, indicating a conserved cellular stress response mechanism.
results.evaluation: Claims C4, C34, C94-C104 demonstrate CD133 induction across multiple cell types (MCF10A: C98; glioblastoma: C99; insulinoma: C100; colon adenocarcinoma: C101; cervical cancer: C102; kidney fibroblasts: C103) using qRT-PCR (C94, C96, C98-C103) and immunoblotting (C94). The rapid and dramatic induction (C97) independent of other stem cell markers (C96) supports the interpretation that this is an inherent cellular response to impaired RTK-Ras-Erk signaling (C95, C104). The consistency across diverse cell types strongly supports the conclusion of a conserved mechanism.

results.result: Super-resolution STORM microscopy and electron microscopy reveal that CD133 localizes to intracellular vesicles (~50 nm) distributed on tubulin filaments that bridge neighboring cells. These vesicles, termed 'intercellsomes', are distinct from exosomes and appear to mediate direct cell-cell communication.
results.evaluation: Claims C6, C7, C117-C133 provide multi-scale imaging evidence from confocal microscopy (C117, C118, C121), STORM super-resolution imaging (C127, C128, C130), and electron microscopy (C133, C135) demonstrating CD133 localization on intracellular vesicles. Co-localization with tubulin (C123, C127, C130) and bridging between cells (C118, C119) support the intercellular communication model. The vesicles are ~50 nm (C135), lack exosome markers (C136, C137), and are primarily intracellular (C132, C133). The convergence of multiple imaging modalities strongly supports the characterization of these structures as a novel vesicle type (C136, C139).

results.result: CD133+ intercellsomes are enriched with mRNAs (particularly immediate early genes like Jun, Junb, Myc) rather than miRNAs, showing selective mRNA inclusion. This RNA composition is markedly different from extracellular vesicles (EVs), which are enriched in miRNAs.
results.evaluation: Claims C8, C36, C142-C152 demonstrate through RNA profiling (C142), qRT-PCR (C144, C146), RNA-seq (C148, C149, C150, C151), and in situ hybridization (C152) that CD133+ vesicles contain predominantly mRNAs with minimal miRNAs. The selective enrichment of IEG transcripts (C144, C151, C152) and lack of housekeeping gene enrichment (C144) support selective mRNA inclusion (C145). The sharp contrast with EVs, which are enriched in miRNAs (C148, C149), clearly distinguishes the two vesicle types. The convergence of multiple RNA analysis methods strongly supports the characterization of intercellsome RNA content.

results.result: CD133+ intercellsomes contain the RNA-binding protein HuR and traffic between neighboring cells, as demonstrated by tracking CD133-Myc fusion proteins. Treatment of cells with isolated CD133+ vesicles enhances cyclin D1 expression, supporting functional cargo transfer.
results.evaluation: Claims C153-C166 provide evidence for intercellsome trafficking through cell mixing experiments with tagged CD133 (C153, C154), CLEM imaging (C155), and immunostaining showing HuR on bridging filaments (C160, C161, C162). The presence of HuR in isolated vesicles (C158, C166) and enhanced cyclin D1 expression upon vesicle treatment (C164) support functional cargo transfer (C165). The selective trafficking of CD133-Myc without GFP/mCherry migration (C154) demonstrates specificity. The convergence of trafficking data and functional assays supports the conclusion of intercellular vesicle transfer.

results.result: Single-cell RNA-seq reveals that Shp2-deficient cells exhibit lower intracellular diversity (entropy) of immediate early genes (IEGs), which is restored in CD133+ cells. Mathematical modeling demonstrates that exchanging 1/12 of IEGs between 4-5 cells twice is sufficient to convert intercellular heterogeneity into intracellular diversity, potentially driving enhanced proliferation.
results.evaluation: Claims C9, C38, C39, C167-C183 present scRNA-seq data showing lower IEG diversity in SKO cells (C38, C176, C177) that is remedied in CD133+ cells (C39, C177, C179). Mathematical modeling (C181, C182) demonstrates that mRNA exchange can reproduce the CD133+ cell profile. However, the causal link between mRNA exchange and the observed entropy changes remains speculative (C10, C40, C168, C169, C183). While the correlation between IEG diversity and proliferation is observed (C180), direct experimental evidence for mRNA exchange (rather than other mechanisms) driving the entropy increase is lacking. The modeling is consistent with the hypothesis but does not prove it. Additional experiments tracking actual mRNA transfer and demonstrating functional consequences are needed to fully support this mechanism.

results.result: CD133 deficiency increases sensitivity to proliferative signal inhibition in both liver (Prom1/Shp2 double knockout) and intestinal organoids (Prom1 KO with MEK inhibitor). CD133 does not function cell-autonomously, as SKO cells in DKO colonies proliferate at DKO levels, supporting a non-cell-autonomous intercellular communication role.
results.evaluation: Claims C11, C12, C184-C196 demonstrate through double knockout experiments (C185, C187) and organoid studies (C194) that CD133 deficiency sensitizes cells to proliferative signal inhibition. The cell mixing experiments (C190) showing SKO cells in DKO colonies proliferate like DKO cells argue against cell-autonomous function and support intercellular communication. The maintained cell-cell contacts in DKO cells (C191) indicate CD133 is not required for adhesion but for communication. The consistency across liver and intestinal models (C194, C195, C196) supports a general functional role. However, the observation that DKO cells still show higher proliferation in colonies than non-colonized cells (C189) suggests CD133 is not the sole mediator, which is appropriately acknowledged.

results.result: Wnt signaling, particularly Wnt10a and PORCN, is upregulated in SKO liver and associated with CD133+ colonies. PORCN inhibition suppresses CD133 induction in MEK inhibitor-treated cells, suggesting Wnt10a plays a role in CD133 induction and potentially colony assembly under proliferative signal deficiency.
results.evaluation: Claims C105-C116 demonstrate through qRT-PCR (C105, C110, C111, C114), immunostaining (C106, C108), and immunoblotting (C109) that Wnt signaling components are upregulated in SKO liver and associated with colonies. The PORCN inhibition experiment (C115) provides functional evidence linking Wnt signaling to CD133 induction (C116). The cellular source of Wnt10a is identified as hepatocytes (C111). However, the role in colony assembly (C107, C113) remains somewhat speculative as direct functional experiments (e.g., Wnt10a knockout or neutralization) are not presented. The data support a role for Wnt signaling in CD133 induction but the mechanistic details of colony formation require further investigation.

results.result: The study unveils a novel CD133-mediated intercellular communication mechanism that compensates for intracellular signal deficits in various cell types. CD133 expression is dynamically regulated by proliferative signaling rather than being strictly associated with cell identity, and this mechanism is likely conserved across cell types for proliferation under stress.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C13, C41, C42, C197-C200, C217 represent the main conclusions synthesizing findings across multiple experiments. The dynamic regulation of CD133 by proliferative signaling (C198) is supported by data from multiple genetic models (C2, C33, C92, C93) and pharmacological inhibition (C4, C94-C104). The intercellular communication mechanism (C13, C41, C197) is supported by vesicle characterization (C6-C8, C127-C139), cargo analysis (C142-C152), trafficking experiments (C153-C155), and functional studies (C185-C196). The conservation across cell types (C199, C217) is demonstrated by experiments in liver, intestinal organoids, and multiple cancer cell lines. The interpretation that this compensates for signal deficits (C13, C42, C200) is supported by the genetic and pharmacological perturbation experiments. These conclusions are well-supported by the collective experimental evidence.

results.result: In Shp2-deficient (SKO) livers following partial hepatectomy (PHx), actively dividing hepatocytes form distinctive clusters characterized by upregulated CD133 expression while remaining negative for other progenitor cell markers. These CD133+ clusters show significantly higher proliferation rates than surrounding areas and are composed of mature hepatocytes rather than hepatoblasts or oval cells.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm this as a primary observation, stating 'the limited regeneration observed in livers with Ras/Erk signaling defects is associated with CD133 expression by groups of cells' and that 'this hepatocyte proliferation is marked by expression of CD133 by groups of cells.' The data are described as 'convincing' by one reviewer.

results.result: CD133+ cell colonies appear transiently following PHx, undergo expansion until 3 weeks, and then merge into surrounding tissues by 5 weeks after PHx with loss of CD133 expression and disappearance of clear colony edges.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not question the temporal dynamics of CD133+ colony formation and resolution. The editor's summary notes these are 'new observations, supported by convincing data,' implicitly accepting the time-course findings.

results.result: Similar CD133+ proliferating hepatocyte clusters are observed in MET-deficient livers following PHx or CCl4 injury, suggesting CD133 induction is a response to impaired proliferative signaling rather than being restricted to a specific gene deletion or injury model.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge these findings across different genetic models and injury types. The consistency across models is implicitly accepted as part of the 'convincing data' noted by reviewers.

results.result: Pharmaceutical inhibition of proliferative signaling (Shp2 or Mek inhibitors) induces CD133 expression in various cancer cell types from multiple organs and species, indicating an inherent cellular response to impaired RTK-Ras-Erk signaling that is rapid, dramatic, and independent of other stem cell markers.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept these findings as part of the 'new observations' with 'broad significance to the fields of regeneration and cancer.' No concerns are raised about the CD133 induction experiments across multiple cell types.

results.result: Clonal tracing experiments using GFP labeling reveal that colonies contain both GFP+ and GFP− cells indicating multiple origins, expand by proliferation of cells from inside rather than continuous recruitment, and that hepatocytes within colonies divide much more actively than those outside. The initial colony size is estimated at approximately 10 hepatocytes.
results.evaluation: One reviewer explicitly questions 'What is the evidence that the observed CD133 groups of cells are not due to clonal growth. Is this conclusion based on the time course (the groups appear more rapidly than proliferation) or is this based on the GFP clonal analysis?' This indicates uncertainty about whether the clonal analysis definitively rules out clonal expansion as the primary mechanism.

results.result: Super-resolution microscopy (STORM) and electron microscopy localize CD133 on intracellular vesicles (named 'intercellsomes') that are tightly associated with tubulin filaments and appear to bridge neighboring cells in colonies, suggesting direct cell-cell communication.
results.evaluation: Reviewers note that 'CD133 appears to be located on intracellular vesicles associated with microtubules' and describe these as 'new observations.' The editor's summary states the study demonstrates 'mRNA-loaded CD133+ intracellular vesicles,' accepting the vesicle characterization.

results.result: Isolated CD133+ intercellsomes are enriched with mRNAs rather than miRNAs, particularly transcripts of immediate early responsive genes (IEGs) such as Jun, Junb, and Myc, showing selective inclusion of mRNAs. This contrasts with EVs/exosomes which are enriched with miRNAs.
results.evaluation: The editor's summary explicitly states 'mRNA-loaded CD133+ intracellular vesicles,' accepting this key finding. Reviewers describe the vesicles as 'loaded with mRNA' without questioning the RNA profiling data.

results.result: CD133+ vesicles do not contain exosome markers (CD9, CD63, CD81) and do not co-localize with endosome markers (RAB5A, RAB7), supporting their identity as a new type of vesicle distinct from classical exosomes, termed 'intercellsomes.'
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept the characterization of these as a distinct vesicle type. One reviewer notes 'In the revised manuscript, the authors more definitively identified the CD133+ vesicles,' indicating acceptance of the vesicle characterization including its distinction from exosomes.

results.result: Cell mixing experiments with CD133-Myc or CD133-GFP fusion proteins demonstrate that CD133-tagged proteins are transported from donor cells to neighboring recipient cells, while GFP and mCherry signals do not migrate between cells, suggesting selective CD133+ vesicle traffic intercellularly.
results.evaluation: One reviewer asks 'What is the evidence that the CD133 vesicles mediate intercellular communication... Is there direct evidence of transfer - for example, the does the GFP clonal analysis show transfer of GFP that is not mediated by clonal proliferation?' While the fusion protein experiments provide some evidence, the reviewer's question indicates uncertainty about whether this definitively demonstrates functional intercellular transfer.

results.result: Single-cell RNA sequencing reveals that Shp2-deficient cells exhibit lower intracellular transcriptional diversity (entropy) of IEGs compared to WT, but CD133+ cells show high intracellular IEG diversity and low intercellular variations. Total IEG levels are higher in WT than SKO cells, and IEG diversity correlates positively with Cyclin D1 expression.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not question the scRNA-seq findings. One reviewer notes the study 'demonstrated that cells defective for proliferative signaling exhibited lower intracellular transcriptional diversity (entropy), which was remedied in CD133+ cells,' accepting these observations.

results.result: Mathematical modeling based on scRNA-seq data suggests that intercellular mRNA exchange between CD133+ cells could convert intercellular heterogeneity into higher intracellular diversity (entropy). Simulations show that exchanging 1/12 of IEGs with four other cells twice is sufficient to reach the distinctive IEG profile of CD133+ cells.
results.evaluation: One reviewer explicitly asks 'Is this inferred from IEG mRNA diversity? or some other data' regarding evidence for intercellular communication, indicating the mathematical modeling and entropy analysis are viewed as indirect evidence rather than direct demonstration. The reviewer requests 'Increased clarity concerning what is hypothesis and what is directly supported by data.'

results.result: In Prom1/Shp2 double knockout (DKO) hepatocytes, proliferation in E-Cad+ colonies is significantly suppressed compared to Shp2 single knockout, while Prom1 KO alone does not inhibit proliferation. Cell mixing experiments show SKO cells in DKO colonies proliferate only as much as DKO cells, arguing against a cell-autonomous role of CD133.
results.evaluation: One reviewer notes 'The functional significance of CD133 was tested using Prom1 KO mice - the data presented are convincing.' Another reviewer states 'The functional significance of CD133 on this cell-cell communication was further demonstrated with genetic knockout studies,' accepting the DKO experiments as demonstrating CD133's role.

results.result: CD133-deficient cells are more sensitive to proliferative signal inhibition in both livers and intestinal organoids. Treatment with Trametinib shows more prominent inhibition of proliferation in Prom1 KO organoids than WT controls.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept the functional validation in multiple systems. One reviewer notes the study 'showed that the induction of CD133 (and by derivative, the CD133+ vesicles) are necessary for maintaining cell proliferation' in both liver and intestinal organoids, accepting these findings.

results.result: HuR, an RNA-binding protein, is loaded in CD133+ vesicles and localizes to the apical side of CD133+ hepatocytes. HuR is visible on CD133+ filaments bridging neighboring cells, and its density on filaments increases with Shp2/Mek inhibitor treatment. Lipofection with CD133+ vesicles enhances cyclin D1 expression.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not question the HuR findings. One reviewer notes 'The authors also provided additional experimental evidence demonstrating the role of these CD133+ vesicles in cell-cell communication,' which would include the HuR and cyclin D1 data.

results.result: Wnt signaling molecules (Wnt7a, Wnt10a, Shh) and Porcupine (PORCN) are upregulated in SKO liver and associated with CD133+ colonies. Wnt10a is mainly produced by hepatocytes and may act as a local inducer of colonies. PORCN inhibition suppresses CD133 induction in Trametinib-treated cells.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge the Wnt signaling data. These findings are treated as supporting mechanistic details that are part of the overall 'convincing data' noted by reviewers.

comparisons.comparison: Both evaluate CD133+ colony formation in Shp2-deficient hepatocytes as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides comprehensive analysis of claims C2, C3, C30, C31, C43-C53 including proliferation markers and time-course data. Peer review focuses on subset C2, C3, C30, C31, C44, C46, C48-C51, C71, describing data as 'convincing' and affirming this as a primary observation. Strong agreement on core findings.

OpenEval evaluates C54-C71 as SUPPORTED, concluding CD133+ colonies consist of mature hepatocytes based on marker expression and morphology. Peer review addresses only temporal dynamics (C32, C60, C61) as SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting time-course findings. Limited overlap; peer review does not explicitly evaluate the mature hepatocyte identity claims that are central to OpenEval R2.

OpenEval evaluates clonal tracing data (C72-C86) as SUPPORTED, concluding colonies form from heterogeneous mature hepatocytes. Peer review evaluates overlapping claims (C73-C79) as UNCERTAIN, explicitly questioning whether clonal analysis definitively rules out clonal expansion. This represents a key disagreement: OpenEval finds evidence sufficient while peer review requests clarification on the interpretation.

Both evaluate CD133+ cluster formation across different injury models and genetic backgrounds as SUPPORTED. OpenEval addresses C87-C93 (CCl4, PHx, MET-deficient models). Peer review addresses C33, C88, C92, C93, implicitly accepting consistency across models as part of 'convincing data.' Strong agreement on generalizability of findings.

Perfect claim overlap (C4, C34, C94-C104). Both evaluate CD133 induction across multiple cell types as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes rapid induction independent of other stem cell markers as evidence of conserved mechanism. Peer review accepts these as 'new observations' with 'broad significance.' Complete agreement on this finding.

Both evaluate CD133 localization on intracellular vesicles as SUPPORTED. OpenEval comprehensively addresses C6, C7, C117-C133 using multi-scale imaging evidence. Peer review addresses subset C6, C7, C117-C119, C121-C123, C127, C133, describing these as 'new observations' and accepting vesicle characterization. Strong agreement on imaging-based vesicle identification.

High claim overlap (11 of 12 claims shared). Both evaluate mRNA content of CD133+ vesicles as SUPPORTED. OpenEval addresses C8, C36, C142-C152 emphasizing selective mRNA enrichment and distinction from EVs. Peer review addresses C8, C36, C142, C144-C152, explicitly stating 'mRNA-loaded CD133+ intracellular vesicles.' Strong agreement on RNA profiling findings.

OpenEval evaluates intercellsome trafficking (C153-C166) as SUPPORTED based on cell mixing, CLEM imaging, and HuR data. Peer review evaluates subset (C153-C155) as UNCERTAIN, explicitly questioning whether there is 'direct evidence of transfer' beyond fusion protein experiments. Disagreement on sufficiency of evidence for functional intercellular transfer.

OpenEval R8 includes HuR and functional cargo transfer data (C153-C166) as part of trafficking evidence, evaluated as SUPPORTED. Peer review R14 separately evaluates HuR findings (C158-C166) as SUPPORTED without questioning. Agreement on HuR data, but peer review separates this from broader trafficking claims that remain uncertain in R9.

OpenEval evaluates scRNA-seq entropy findings and mRNA exchange mechanism (C9, C38, C39, C167-C183) as UNCERTAIN, noting causal link remains speculative. Peer review evaluates scRNA-seq observations (C9, C38, C39, C171, C176, C177, C179, C180) as SUPPORTED but does not address mathematical modeling claims. Partial agreement: both accept entropy observations, but OpenEval explicitly flags mechanistic interpretation as uncertain.

OpenEval R9 includes mathematical modeling (C181-C183) as part of UNCERTAIN evaluation of mRNA exchange mechanism. Peer review R11 evaluates modeling and entropy analysis (C10, C40, C168, C169, C181, C182, C183, C207, C208) as UNCERTAIN, requesting clarity on 'what is hypothesis and what is directly supported.' Strong agreement that modeling provides indirect rather than direct evidence.

OpenEval evaluates CD133 functional role via DKO experiments (C11, C12, C184-C196) as SUPPORTED. Peer review R12 evaluates subset (C185, C186, C187, C190, C191) as SUPPORTED, describing data as 'convincing' and accepting that genetic knockout demonstrates CD133's role. Strong agreement on functional validation through DKO experiments.

OpenEval R10 includes organoid validation (C11, C12, C194-C196) as part of SUPPORTED functional evidence. Peer review R13 separately evaluates organoid findings (C11, C12, C194, C195) as SUPPORTED, accepting functional validation in multiple systems. Strong agreement on conservation across liver and intestinal models.

High claim overlap (11 of 12 claims shared). OpenEval evaluates Wnt signaling data (C105-C116) as SUPPORTED but notes mechanistic details of colony formation remain somewhat speculative. Peer review evaluates same claims as SUPPORTED without raising concerns, treating as supporting mechanistic details. Minor difference in confidence level regarding mechanistic interpretation.

OpenEval R12 synthesizes main conclusions (C1, C13, C41, C42, C197-C200, C217) as SUPPORTED, integrating findings across all experiments. No corresponding peer review result explicitly evaluates these synthetic conclusion claims, though individual supporting findings are addressed in other peer review results.

Peer review R2 evaluates temporal dynamics (C32, C60, C61) as SUPPORTED, accepting time-course findings. These claims are included in OpenEval R1 (C50, C51) and R2 (C60, C61) but not isolated as a separate result. Agreement on findings, different grouping strategy.

These claims are included in OpenEval R6 as part of broader vesicle characterization but not isolated. Agreement on vesicle distinction, different result organization.
